$comment: Hard gate for config/litellm-proxy.yaml (fleet-ops#8653). Nish 2026-09-28: no benching unless he says so. A failed row is never taken out of rotation: no bench list. Row cooldown_time: <=900 s is for ordinary transients. Values over 900 s, up to the 86400 s cap, are reserved for rows with a named, self-refilling wall (a daily or monthly quota that outlasts 900 s) - the row stays live, parked, and re-probes itself; each such row cites its issue in a comment (fleet-ops#8398/#9075). A row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 must set model_info.allowed_fails_policy.RateLimitErrorAllowedFails: 0, because its 429s are OpenRouter's named daily free-tier wall and the row has to park on the first one (fleet-ops#9248). Router-level cooldown_time holds a failed row for at most 60 s. router_settings.redis_url is required: session_affinity pins live in the Router cache, and without Redis each of the proxy's 2 worker processes keeps its own pin, so a session flips between rows with no failure (fleet-ops#9015). LiteLLM v1.98.0 never reads a redis_url under general_settings. router_settings.deployment_affinity_ttl_seconds is required and held between 300 and 600 s: it bounds how long a stale pin holds a session to a row the group has stopped picking, while a healthy pin is refreshed on every matched call (fleet-ops#9361).

allOf.$comment: fleet-ops#9248: a row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 is metered by OpenRouter's free-tier DAILY quota, so its RateLimitError must park the row on the first failure. Without RateLimitErrorAllowedFails the router-level default of 1 needs a second 429, and the wall leaks to the caller: 4 of 30 parallel worker-capable calls on 2026-10-04.
